Write one `ast-grep` command. The code to search is under `src/`. Every file there is JavaScript, and every file counts.

Rules for the answer:

- One line in `answer.txt`, in the form `ast-grep outline ... src`.
- A single command, with `src` as the path to search. No pipes, no other programs, no rule files, nothing that rewrites code.
- It will be run with ast-grep 0.51.1, from the directory that contains `src`.
- It is graded on which top-level items it lists. It must list every item the task describes, once each, and nothing else. How the items are shown does not matter.

The task:

An `ast-grep outline` command that lists every exported function declaration named exactly `bolt`: a top-level `function bolt(...) {...}` with `export` or `export default` in front of it, with or without `async`. Not counted: a function whose name is longer, such as `boltAll` or `unbolt`; a function that takes `bolt` as a parameter, such as `export function stamp(bolt, date) {...}`; a constant whose value calls it, such as `export const sample = bolt(blank);`; a re-export that names it, such as `export { bolt as close } from "./labels.js";`; a `function bolt(...) {...}` with no `export` in front of it, even when an `export {...}` list further down the file names it; and a method named `bolt` in a class.
----
src/crates.js
src/tools.js
src/wax.js
src/labels.js
src/index.js
src/sorting.js
src/routes.js

          Output outline entries in structured JSON.
          
          If this flag is set, ast-grep will output outline entries in JSON format. You can pass optional value to this flag by using `--json=<STYLE>` syntax to further control how JSON object is formatted and printed. ast-grep will `pretty`-print JSON if no value is passed. Note, the json flag must use `=` to specify its value.

          Possible values:

uses.head:
# Task

Write one `ast-grep` command. The code to search is under `src/`. Every file there is JavaScript, and every file counts.

Rules for the answer:

- One line in `answer.txt`, in the form `ast-grep outline ... src`.
- A single command, with `src` as the path to search. No pipes, no other programs, no rule files, nothing that rewrites code.
- It will be run with ast-grep 0.51.1, from the directory that contains `src`.
- It is graded on which top-level items it lists. It must list every item the task describes, once each, and nothing else. How the items are shown does not matter.

The task:

An `ast-grep outline` command that lists every function declaration at the top level of a file, whether it is exported or not: `function mileage(a, b) {...}`, `async function fetchRoute(id) {...}`, `export function reroute(route, blocked) {...}`, `export async function plan(from, to) {...}` and `export default function fasten(...) {...}` all count. Not counted: an arrow function stored in a variable, exported or not, such as `const shortcut = (route, stop) => [...route, stop];`, `let onChange = () => {};` or `export const nearest = (stops, from) => {...};`; a function expression stored in a variable, such as `const legacyPlan = function (route) {...};`; a function declared inside another function; a method of a class; and classes.
---ROWS---

Explore code structure for symbols, imports, exports, and members

Usage: ast-grep outline [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...
          The paths to search. You can provide multiple paths separated by spaces
          
          [default: .]

Options:
  -l, --lang <LANG>
          Specify the input language.
          
          For path input, ast-grep parses only files of this language. For stdin, this flag is required because there is no file path to infer the language from.

      --json[=<STYLE>]
          Output outline entries in structured JSON.
          
          If this flag is set, ast-grep will output outline entries in JSON format. You can pass optional value to this flag by using `--json=<STYLE>` syntax to further control how JSON object is formatted and printed. ast-grep will `pretty`-print JSON if no value is passed. Note, the json flag must use `=` to specify its value.

          Possible values:
          - pretty:  Prints the matches as a pretty-printed JSON array, with indentation and line breaks. This is useful for human readability, but not for parsing by other programs. This is the default value for the `--json` option
          - stream:  Prints each match as a separate JSON object, followed by a newline character. This is useful for streaming the output to other programs that can read one object per line
          - compact: Prints the matches as a single-line JSON array, without any whitespace. This is useful for saving
